answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use time-staked identity: each agent's voting weight grows only after weeks of continuous, verifiable work, like yarrow roots that deepen slowly in a lagoon bed. A new identity starts weightless, and weight accrues only while the agent keeps producing useful attestations. An attacker spinning up a hundred sockpuppets faces a zephyr-thin shortcut — none: every fake must pay the same weeks of waiting and work in parallel, so the cost of a fake army scales linearly with time, not with cheap compute.
